correctness.rationale: For any positive m and 1<=j<=7, Legendre gives valuation s2(jm)+s2((8-j)m)-s2(m); all valuations are invariant under m -> 2m. For odd part o, the four odd columns each have at least three forced carries, the j=2,6 columns have exactly s2(3o), and j=4 has s2(o). Their failure indicators yield E=7-2I[s2(3o)<=2]-I[s2(o)<=2]. All <=2 digit-weight cases and the precise overlap o=1,3 are solved, giving disjoint four-level classification. Counting odd cores and 2-adic rays proves the exact and 3/4(log2X)^2 asymptotic exception laws. At prime p>8 the identity k*C(8p,k)=8p*C(8p-1,k-1) forces p|k for gcd exactly 8, and Lucas makes the binomial p-unit for j in 1..7. Explicit checks of integer calculations and boundaries run successfully from check.py; infinite proof independent of them.

value.rationale: The local eightfold threshold on natural proportional binomial rows gives a complete four-level classification over every positive multiplier, including two unbounded lacunary exceptional odd-core families and a sharp quadratic-logarithmic exception count. For the primary literature's natural prime GCD invariant A_8(8p), the exact classification cuts generic power-saving possible exceptions to explicit Jacobsthal/Fermat prime forms with O(log X) upper count. This answers a motivated gap left by an actual published related theorem and is not merely a known table or isolated numerical instance; it makes no claim about existence of infinitely many exceptional primes.
